epics.title: Production Data Binding and Mock Eradication
epics.jtbd: When I browse the site as a visitor, I want to see only real, published content from the author, so that I experience their actual thoughts without placeholder data.
requirements: R1: The frontend fetches all list and detail views exclusively from the live backend APIs.
R2: All mock data, hardcoded test items, fake profiles, and placeholder texts are completely removed from the frontend codebase.
R3: When an API returns no data, the UI displays a proper, localized Russian empty state message rather than a generic or fake placeholder.
R4: The site dynamically displays the actual count of published podcast episodes, sourced from the API.
R5: The system strictly filters content to ensure raw teleprompter drafts are never exposed to the public UI.

R6: COMPLETENESS FLOOR EXCLUSION: The standard 'Content management and publishing' chain (draft -> edit -> approve -> publish -> unpublish) is excluded from this epic because the brief explicitly states content is ingested via external systems (Telegram, Headless API) and not through a CMS built here.

epics.title: Sovereign Canon and Ontology Architecture
epics.jtbd: When a visitor explores the site, I want to read the Evergreen manifestos and ontology across structured domains, so that I understand the core architectural philosophy.
requirements: R1: The Canon concept is presented as a primary entity with bidirectional cross-links to podcast episodes, essays, and short notes (sparks).
R2: The site features an instant search accessible via Cmd+K / Ctrl+K, allowing keyboard-driven, semantic search across the entire content corpus without page reloads.
R3: Every content node provides a permanent human-readable URL.
R4: Every content node provides machine-readable formats (llms.txt, ai-agent.json, Markdown/JSON) exposing semantic relationships to AI agents.
R5: The relationship graph of concepts and content is stored in and served from the backend database, not hardcoded in the frontend.
R6: The UI allows the author to quickly search and retrieve their own concepts for frictionless note-taking and reference.

R7: COMPLETENESS FLOOR EXCLUSION: Standard editorial chains for managing this graph (drafting, publishing) are excluded as this epic focuses purely on the architecture and frontend navigation of the graph; content ingestion is handled by other epics.

epics.title: Black-Box Public Facade
epics.jtbd: When I visit the public site, I want to experience a clean reading environment, so that I am focused on ideas without being distracted by internal tools.
requirements: R1: The 'Studio and Setup' tab and all associated workspace/studio imagery are completely removed from the public frontend.
R2: All links to the /admin path and references to factory internals (internal orchestrators, system tags) are removed from the public footer and navigation.
R3: The visual design adheres strictly to the Modern Swiss Editorial aesthetic, avoiding popups and ensuring a clean monochromatic presentation.
R4: COMPLETENESS FLOOR EXCLUSION: Standard client portal chains (sign in, manage state) are intentionally excluded because the public facade is purely a reader view without user accounts.

epics.title: Platform Telemetry and Measurement
epics.jtbd: When operating the site, I want to measure visitor engagement with my content and external links, so that I know if the site successfully drives interest in my work.
requirements: R1: The system captures the goal: 'Is the site successfully conveying the author's extended mind and engaging readers with the Canon?'
R2: The system measures Q1: 'Are visitors traversing the knowledge graph by clicking cross-links between essays, podcasts, and canon nodes?'
R3: The system measures Q2: 'Are visitors utilizing the Cmd+K search to find specific concepts?'
R4: The telemetry is strictly limited to these core behavioral questions, ignoring vanity metrics.

epics.title: Privacy Consent Management
epics.jtbd: When a visitor arrives on the site, I want to be asked for consent before any non-essential trackers load, so that my privacy preferences are respected and the site complies with ePrivacy regulations.
requirements: R1: A consent banner appears before any non-essential telemetry or tracker is loaded.
R2: The user can refuse tracking just as easily as accepting it, with a single click.
R3: The user's consent choice is recorded and can be revoked later.
R4: The consent mechanism uses an established, compliant consent platform rather than a custom widget.

epics.title: Data Protection and Recovery
epics.jtbd: When the database experiences a failure, I want to be able to restore the system state from a backup, so that I do not lose my published content.
requirements: R1: The database containing the author's published work and relationship graph is backed up regularly on an automated schedule.
R2: A full backup restoration process is documented and has been practically verified to ensure availability after an incident.

epics.title: Headless Content Management API for AI Agents
epics.jtbd: When operating the site, I want external AI agents to autonomously manage content via secure headless APIs, so that materials are updated dynamically without exposing the codebase or infrastructure.
requirements: R1: The system exposes a secure headless API allowing the author or an authorized AI agent to publish new essays or canon concepts.
R2: Content ingested via the headless API appears on the live site automatically, without requiring any manual redeployment or file changes.
R3: The API operates strictly at the content layer; it provides no access to infrastructure, code, or administrative controls.
R4: COMPLETENESS FLOOR: This covers the 'author -> publish -> update' chain explicitly required by the brief for the headless ingestion mechanism.
